Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 97, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Qadr (the Decree), because of the repeated mention of Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) in it, the night in which the revelation of the Qur'an began. It is a blessed night of great worth.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Highlighting the virtue and greatness of the Qur'an by attributing its revelation to Allah, the Exalted; highlighting the virtue of the time of its revelation; and explaining the excellence of Laylat al-Qadr in the month of Ramadan, and the reward of righteous deeds performed in it.

[The Exegesis]

Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Honour and Excellence, which is one of the nights of the month of Ramadan.
And what will make you know, O Prophet, what the Night of Decree is, with its honor and status?

Laylat al-Qadr is a blessed night; good deeds performed in it are better than the deeds of a thousand months in which there is no Laylat al-Qadr. This is a favor from Allah, the Exalted, upon this nation.
The Angels and the Spirit descend therein in abundance, by the permission of their Lord, with every decree He has ordained for that year.
It is all security, with no evil in it until the break of dawn.
